A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ULTHO work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching v1's final appendix to Appendix E in v2.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original ULTHO and Relay-ULTHO experiments on ALE, Procgen, MiniGrid, and PyBullet. Some comparator results are borrowed, but the proposed methods' evaluations are original.

after.justification: Retains the original empirical results and adds an equal-budget comparison, search-space sensitivity experiments, and SAC+ULTHO results on two DMC tasks in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Appendix D introduces an off-policy adaptation that selects a hyperparameter every T steps and evaluates its utility using windowed averages of batch action values Q(s,a). The original on-policy procedure and Relay-ULTHO remain unchanged; Section 4's Q-to-U relabeling and equation reordering clarify their presentation.

E1.justification: Adds the DMC continuous-control tasks Hopper Hop and Quadruped Run in Figure 23. The existing ALE-5, sixteen Procgen environments, three MiniGrid tasks, and four PyBullet tasks are retained.

E2.justification: SAC is newly evaluated against SAC+ULTHO in Figure 23. Comparator membership in the retained ALE comparison and Procgen Table 1 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds a separate ALE-5 comparison with an equal 100M-step budget per method, alongside the retained unequal-budget comparison. It also introduces experiments with 2, 3, 4, or 6 clusters, 2, 3, or 4 values per cluster, and a SAC/DMC evaluation. These substantially extend the evaluation design; Appendix B's original settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained exploration-coefficient and sliding-window sensitivity studies, Figures 21–22 test whether the advantage survives equal training budgets and how performance depends on cluster count and candidate granularity. These add substantive controls and analyses of the search-space design.

E5.justification: Existing seed counts and mean, standard-error, and standard-deviation reporting are retained. The new appendix includes error bars and shaded bands but introduces no specified new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test, or increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Original scores and plotted results are retained. Figures 21–23 add an equal-budget advantage over HPO baselines, higher Procgen aggregates with four versus two clusters but no further gain with six, task-dependent effects of candidate counts, and higher final SAC+ULTHO returns on both DMC tasks. These are new findings under additional conditions, not improvements to the retained results.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 expands the discount-factor interval from [0,1) to [0,1]. Appendix D adds a mathematical definition of off-policy utility using batch action values. The original UCB mathematics is otherwise equivalent after relabeling and reordering; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and Discussion retain the same headline claims about lightweight, adaptive HPO through clustered bandits, the two ULTHO algorithms, and effectiveness across the original benchmarks. The added experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D attributes the equal-budget advantage to frequent tuning and limited benefits from larger search spaces to MAB capacity. It also newly advises against off-policy use because replay-buffer return estimates can be unstable. Existing limitations concerning categorical search and alternative bandit strategies remain.

D1.justification: The abstract and footnote newly state that ULTHO code is available and provide a repository link. Existing implementation sources and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. Documentation of the new experiments is limited, including no numerical SAC tuning interval T or complete configurations for the expanded search spaces.

R1.justification: Adds references to Soft Actor-Critic and the DeepMind Control Suite for the new off-policy experiment. Existing related-work coverage and positioning remain substantively unchanged; most citation-number changes simply accommodate these additions.

P1.justification: Makes localized wording corrections, reorganizes Section 4.1 around utility notation and episode indexing, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgements and Appendix D. The former decision-process Appendix D becomes Appendix E. The overall narrative and main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Adds Figures 21–23 with budget-comparison bars, search-space sensitivity panels, and SAC learning curves. Original Figures 21–22 are retained as Figures 24–25. Equation annotations, some captions, and text placement change, while the original figure graphics and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: Appendix D supplies useful equal-budget and search-space controls missing from v1, while the SAC experiment adds evidence with an explicit applicability warning. Clearer method exposition and code-access information also help. The overall gain is limited by sparse documentation of the new configurations and uncertainty displays, particularly the unspecified SAC tuning interval and tested hyperparameter values.
